name: .40 Smith Pattern
description:
The .40 Smith Pattern takes its name not from a manufacturer — there has been no Smith & Wesson for over a century — but from the historical designation of the .40 S&W cartridge that serves as its dimensional ancestor. By 2200 the name has passed into generic usage, the way 'Kleenex' meant tissue paper or 'Xerox' meant photocopy in an earlier age. In GLMZ, '.40 Smith Pattern' or just 'Smith Load' means a .40-caliber semi-automatic pistol cartridge, regardless of who made it, and several manufacturers including Arcturus Defense Solutions' civilian division and Slagworks' mid-tier Irongate Premium line produce it in both brass-cased and caseless variants.

The .40 Smith Pattern has a complicated reputation in GLMZ's firearms culture. It was the dominant law enforcement cartridge of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, associated with a police establishment that no longer exists in any recognizable form. Some mid-tier shooters find that history interesting; others find it irrelevant; a small contingent of Tier 1 veterans who remember the old Meridian PD find it actively distasteful. What is undeniable is that the round delivers meaningfully more energy than 9x19mm from the same platform size, at the cost of sharper recoil and slightly reduced magazine capacity. In 2200's threat environment, where subdermal augmentation has pushed the performance ceiling for what a standard nine needs to defeat, the extra mass of the .40 SP has given it a renewed relevance among shooters who take the math seriously.
compatibility_note: Compatible with semi-automatic pistols chambered for .40 S&W or .40 Smith Pattern spec. Moderate platform availability in GLMZ — not as widespread as 9x19mm but with solid support from ADS civilian division and Slagworks Irongate Premium. Caseless variant available in modern spec platforms. Not compatible with 9x19mm or .45 chambers without conversion.
reliability_note: Very reliable in brass-cased configuration. Operates at higher pressure than 9x19mm, which demands slightly more attentive maintenance, but modern production .40 SP is consistent and dependable. Functions across GLMZ's full environmental range. No energy dependency. Caseless variant is reliable in platforms designed for it. Recoil-operated cycling is robust; fewer feeding issues than some high-pressure semi-auto rounds.
